unit.title: Staying alive
unit.blurb: Our organs, animal groups and life cycles, food chains and fossils.

O1.t: Name the heart, lungs, brain and stomach and say what each organ does.

O2.t: Sort animals into groups, and describe simple life cycles (chicken, frog, butterfly).

O3.t: Read and build simple food chains that start with a plant.

O4.t: Know that fossils are remains of living things from long ago, and that extinct means none are left.

captions: Hello, little scientists!
Inside your body there are amazing parts that keep you alive!
This is lesson 4.1: our organs.
Your body is busy all day and all night.
Inside your body there are special parts called organs.
Each organ has an important job.
Let's meet some of them!
Your heart pumps blood all around your body.
Your lungs breathe air in and out.
Your brain helps you think, learn and remember.
And your stomach holds the food you eat.
Pause and think.
Which organ pumps blood around your body?
Put your hand on your chest. Feel that?
Thump, thump, thump. That is your heart beating!
Now jump up and down ten times.
Feel again. Your heart is beating faster!
Now take a deep breath in.
Your chest gets bigger, like a balloon. Your lungs are filling with air!
Now breathe out slowly.
Your lungs work all the time, even when you sleep.
Did you know?
Make a fist with your hand.
Your heart is about the same size as your fist!
Joke time!
Why did the heart go to the disco?
Because it had a great beat!
Your turn.
Which organ do you think with?
Let's do a heartbeat test.
Sit still, and feel your heartbeat on your chest. Is it fast or slow?
Now jump for one minute.
Feel your heartbeat again. Is it faster or slower?
Let's remember.
Organs are parts inside your body that do important jobs.
Your heart pumps blood.
Your lungs breathe air.
And your brain helps you think. Heart-warming work!

captions: Hello, little scientists!
Animals come in groups. And they all grow up in different ways!
This is lesson 4.2: animal groups and life cycles.
We sort animals into groups.
Mammals have fur or hair. Dogs, cats and people are mammals!
Birds have feathers and wings.
Fish have fins and scales. Reptiles, like snakes, have dry, scaly skin.
Pause and think.
Which animal is a bird?
Animals grow and change. This is called a life cycle.
A hen lays an egg.
A fluffy chick hatches out of the egg.
The chick grows into a hen. Then she lays eggs too!
A frog has an amazing life cycle.
It starts as a tiny egg, in a jelly called frogspawn.
A tadpole hatches. It swims with a tail, like a little fish.
Then it grows legs, loses its tail, and becomes a frog. Ribbit!
A butterfly starts as a tiny egg on a leaf.
A caterpillar hatches. It eats and eats and eats!
It makes a hard case called a chrysalis, and waits inside.
Then out comes a beautiful butterfly!
Did you know?
A whale lives in the sea, but it is not a fish.
It is a mammal! It breathes air, and feeds its babies milk.
Joke time!
What do you call a dinosaur that is fast asleep?
A dino-snore!
Your turn.
What does a tadpole grow into?
Let's make a life cycle wheel.
Get a paper plate, and draw four pictures round the edge.
Draw an egg, a tadpole, a froglet with legs, and a frog.
Add arrows to show how it goes round and round!
Let's remember.
Animals are sorted into groups, like mammals, birds and fish.
Mammals have fur. Birds have feathers. Fish have fins.
A life cycle is how an animal grows and changes.
A tadpole grows into a frog. Wild work, little scientists!

captions: Hello, little scientists!
Who eats who? Let's follow the food!
This is lesson 4.3: food chains.
All animals need food.
Food gives them energy to move and grow.
A rabbit eats plants, like grass and carrots.
Yum, yum!
Grass grows using sunlight.
A rabbit eats the grass.
A fox eats the rabbit.
This is a food chain! It shows who eats what.
Pause and think.
In this food chain, what does the rabbit eat?
We draw food chains with arrows.
The arrow means 'is eaten by'.
A leaf is eaten by a caterpillar.
The caterpillar is eaten by a bird.
Every food chain starts with a plant.
Plants do not eat other living things.
They use sunlight to make their own food.
Then animals eat the plants!
Did you know?
In the sea, tiny plants are eaten by small fish.
And small fish are eaten by big sharks!
Joke time!
Why did the cow cross the road?
To get to the udder side!
Your turn.
What is at the start of every food chain?
Let's make a food chain paper chain!
Cut three strips of paper.
Draw a plant on one, a rabbit on one, and a fox on one.
Loop them together in the right order. Now read your food chain!
Let's remember.
Animals need food for energy.
A food chain shows who eats what.
The arrow means 'is eaten by'.
And every food chain starts with a plant. Tasty work!

captions: Hello, little scientists!
How do we know about dinosaurs? Let's dig in!
This is lesson 4.4: fossils.
Dinosaurs lived a long, long time ago.
Millions and millions of years ago!
No people were alive then.
So how do we know about dinosaurs?
We know because of fossils.
Long ago, an animal died, and mud covered its bones.
Over a very long time, the mud turned into hard rock.
The shape of the bones was kept in the rock. That is a fossil!
Pause and think.
What is a fossil?
There are many kinds of fossils.
Fossil bones and teeth.
Fossil shells.
Even fossil footprints and leaves!
Scientists who study fossils dig very carefully.
They use small brushes to sweep away the dust.
They put the bones together like a puzzle.
Then we can see what the dinosaur looked like!
Did you know?
Dinosaurs are extinct.
That means there are no dinosaurs alive today. We only find their fossils.
Joke time!
What do you call a dinosaur that keeps trying again and again?
A try-ceratops!
Your turn.
What does extinct mean?
Let's make a pretend fossil!
Flatten some play dough or clay.
Press a shell or a toy dinosaur's foot into it, then lift it out.
Look! The shape stays behind, just like a fossil.
Let's remember.
A fossil is the remains of a living thing, kept in rock.
Fossils take millions of years to form.
Fossils tell us about dinosaurs and other animals from long ago.
Extinct means there are none left alive. Dino-mite work!
